text.p: Brierley Investments Ltd said on Monday it was confident it could unlock the value in newspaper publisher John Fairfax Holdings Ltd which has lured media tycoons such as Rupert Murdoch and Conrad Black onto the share register in recent years.

A combination of market and political events mean that only local mogul Kerry Packer is left on the register -- and second in size to Brierley which earlier revealed it had bought a 20 percent stake from Black for A$447.1 million.

The New Zealand based company, which is regarded by many analysts as a near-to-medium term investor which trades companies rather than manages them, has the option to buy Black's other five percent stake for another A$106.7 million.
"I don't think you have seen a fair reflection of what the underlying earnings can be in this company," Rod Price, an executive director of Brierley, told Reuters.
Price said he hoped Rupert Murdoch's description of Fairfax's classified advertising as "rivers of gold" was correct.

"I think it really has got an outstanding franchise in terms of its assets," he said, attributing the poor profit performance of Fairfax in the past year to high paper prices, a weak domestic economy, and management turmoil.

Murdoch, who sold his five percent stake last month and already controls more than half of the country's metropolitan circulation through The News Corp Ltd papers, coined the phrase in reference to the dominant position of the Fairfax newspapers in classified advertising in the key markets of Sydney and Melbourne.
Fairfax owns the Sydney Morning Herald and Melbourne Age broadsheet dailies as well as the daily Australian Financial Review newspaper and a swag of magazines and regional papers.

Price said Fairfax had a great outlook and Brierley would make sure this forecast was achieved by taking a hands-on approach to its new investment. "With this sort of money involved we would never be a passive shareholder."

Price will talk with Fairfax chairman Sir Laurence Street about the appointment of himself and Sir Roger Douglas to the Fairfax board -- the same number of positions as Black's Hollinger International Inc had.

"We are happy in principle with the management team, which overall we think is extremely good," said Price of the company which has had three managing directors in two years and is now led by former News Corp executive Bob Muscat.

Price said Brierley, which is a major shareholder in a variety of regional companies including Air New Zealand Ltd, retailer Coles Myer Ltd and building products company James Hardie Industries Ltd, had a long term commitment to Fairfax.

"The concept of us doing these quick-turns (asset sales) is the odd exception -- but most people don't think of all the others. I can give you numerous examples of where long-term is many, many years -- where we put in the money to help them, we provide financial strength."

Price said Conrad Black, who said earlier this year he wanted permission from the Australian government to increase his Fairfax stake to around 50 percent to ensure control, had made it clear when taking over London's London's Telegraph Plc that he might be a seller if his stake could not be increased.
"We didn't have any unique knowledge that other people couldn't get, it was all there in the (Hollinger) prospectus."
Nor did Brierley view the purchase of Black's stake as a stepping stone to eventual full control.

"We haven't bought this holding on the assumption that it is going to be open-slather with the media review. We are sure there are going to be some changes but we haven't taken a punt on them," he said.

The Australian government's media review now underway is considering possible changes to industry rules which prevent foreigners from holding more than 15 percent of a company and television station proprietors such as Packer from also holding more than 15 percent of a paper in the same market.
Packer, whose holding in Fairfax is just under 15 percent, owns the market-leading Nine television network but has said he would like to merge Fairfax with his own companies.
